To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of the Inception-v4 architecture for the regression problem of plant count yields a MAPE of 6.7%; 2) the use of a CNN trained with a dataset of 10,000 plots yields a MAPE that is 2.7 times lower than a CNN trained with the same number of images of the entire field, which is the most common approach;

(i) the Inception-v2 and Inception-v3 architectures are the most accurate for this task; (ii) the best accuracy is obtained when using the entire image of the crop field; (iii) the best accuracy for a single plot is obtained when using a 512x512 pixel image; (iv) using a 256x256 pixel image results in an accuracy that is 2% lower than that of the 512x512 image.
we have shown that we can count crop plants in an orthorectificated image of a field using a regression approach and the Inception-v4 CNN architecture.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) The use of regression instead of classification for the task of plant counting, (2) the extraction of plots from orthorectified UAV images, (3) the use of a CNN for plant counting and (4) the evaluation of the performance of the CNN for the task of counting plants.
the following tasks: (i) Counting plants in a field, (ii) Extracting images of sections or "plots" from a field image and (iii) Using deep learning for plant counting.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of using CNNs for counting plants using a UAV.
the Inception-v2 architecture is the best choice for this task.
our approach is a good starting point for the problem of counting plants from aerial images, but there is still a long way to go to achieve a robust, reliable and efficient system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to estimate the number of plants in a plot with a MAPE of 6.7%, which is a promising result.
we can count the number of plants in a field with a MAPE of 6.7%.
we can use CNNs for counting plants in an agricultural field with an accuracy of 93% and a MAPE of 6.7%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use CNNs to estimate the number of plants in a field from UAV imagery.
we have demonstrated that deep learning can be used to count plants in a field with a reasonable level of accuracy.
